channel.description: All the news that's fit to reduce

item.title: No. 44: ETH falls. Brute force keeps its job
item.description: Two analyses of the claimed October 2026 refutations of ETH find that the subexponential #3-SAT bounds certify no speed-up over brute force for any bounded-density input that could ever be written down, cut one algorithm's crossover point to about \(2^{420}\) clauses at clause density one, and observe that the Sparse Max-3-SAT Hypothesis falls too; a third paper, an AI-assisted exposition, explains how the counting procedure works.

item.title: No. 43: 4n! Gate Elimination Smashes Through
item.description: Mishra and Santhanam prove that every Boolean circuit over the full binary basis \(B_2\) computing a certain explicit function in \(\mathrm{P}\) needs at least \(4n-O(\log n)\) gates, up from the \(3.5n-o(n)\) in the paper's own earlier version.
